what: The QR Code Generator turns any text or link into a QR code, the square black-and-white pattern that phones can scan with the camera. The code updates live as you type, and you can download it as a PNG image in three sizes.

Small businesses use QR codes on menus, flyers, posters, business cards and product labels to send people to a website, a review page or a payment page. Teachers put them on worksheets, event organisers on tickets and signs, and anyone can use one to share a long link or a short message without typing.
The code is drawn in your browser and the text you type is not sent anywhere.
uses: Print a code on a flyer or poster so people can open your site, menu or sign-up form with one scan.
Put a code on each table that opens your online menu.
Add a code with your website or online profile link to a card or email signature.
Encode a short message, an address, a Wi-Fi password or a serial number as plain text.
Link to a map, schedule or registration page at an event.
tutorial: Click the "Text or link" box. It starts with https://example.com as a sample. Replace it with your own link or text. For a website, include https:// at the start so phones open it as a link.
The QR code below redraws every time you change the text. More text makes a denser code with more, smaller squares.
In "Size" choose 256 px, 512 px (default) or 1024 px. This sets the size of the downloaded PNG image. Use 1024 px for print, and 256 or 512 px for screens and web pages.

In "Error correction" choose Low, Medium (default), High or Highest. Higher levels let the code still scan if part of it is dirty, scratched or covered, but they make the pattern denser and hold less text.
Point your phone camera at the code on the screen. It should show your link or text. Always test before you print many copies.
Click "Download PNG" to save qr-code.png. The image has a white border (quiet zone) around the code, which scanners need, so do not crop it off.
features: The code changes as you type, so you see the result immediately.
Encode URLs, plain text, numbers, and letters from any language.
Low, Medium, High and Highest let you trade capacity for toughness.
A white margin is added around the code so it scans reliably.
The text is stored inside the image itself, with no tracking link in between.

example.title: Worked example: a code for a café menu
example.text: Your menu is at https://mycafe.example/menu. You paste that link into the "Text or link" box. You choose 1024 px because the code will be printed on table cards, and High error correction because cards can get coffee stains. You scan the screen with your phone and the menu opens. Then you click "Download PNG" and place qr-code.png on your card design at least 3 cm wide.

tips: Shorter text makes a simpler code that scans faster and from further away. Use a short link if your URL is very long.
Print the code at least 2 to 3 cm wide, and bigger if people will scan it from a distance, such as on a poster.
Keep strong contrast: dark code on a light background. Do not print it on a busy picture.
Choose High or Highest for codes printed on things that may get scratched or dirty, like stickers and packaging.
Rename the downloaded file after saving if you make several codes, so you do not mix them up.
A printed code cannot be changed later, so double-check the link for typos before printing.
problems: "That text is too long for a QR code."
A QR code has a size limit, and higher error correction leaves less room. Shorten the text, use a shorter link, or pick a lower error correction level.
The phone does not open the link
Make sure the text starts with https:// or http://. Without it, many phones show it as plain text.
The code may be too small, blurry, low contrast or cropped. Print it larger, keep the white border, and use the 1024 px download for print.
The text box is empty. Type something first; the button needs a code to save.
